statement: 2 is a square in Q_p exactly when p = 1 or 7 mod 8 (p odd); computed for the odd primes 3 to 97, argued for every larger p.
argument: A family, one script line per member: `legendre 2 with p` prints the Legendre symbol (2 | p) (tools/adf/README.md:657), and the expected line is 1 when p = 1 or 7 mod 8, else -1. For odd p, 2 is a unit of Z_p, and a unit is a square in Q_p exactly when it is a square mod p (refs/src/conrad-hensel/hensel.txt:160-169, Example 2.9). 2 is a square mod p exactly when p = 1 or 7 mod 8 (refs/src/shoup-ntb/ntb-v2.txt:15017, Theorem 12.1 (iv), and 15032-15034). The computed primes check the rule; the cited sources argue it for every odd p.
